candidate_relations.label: Sarcoma
candidate_relations.reason: The histology and immunoprofile (α-SMA, vimentin, desmin positive; EBV negative; malignant spindle cells) specifically indicate leiomyosarcoma. 'Sarcoma' is the correct family but lacks the required smooth muscle subtype specificity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Sarcoma is the parent category; leiomyosarcoma is a specific smooth muscle sarcoma subtype confirmed by actin/vimentin/desmin positivity

candidate_relations.label: Hemangiopericytoma
candidate_relations.reason: While hemangiopericytoma can present as a vascular meningeal mass, the immunostaining pattern (desmin and α-SMA positivity) is characteristic of smooth muscle differentiation (leiomyosarcoma), not hemangiopericytoma, making this an incompatible subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hemangiopericytoma is a vascular/pericytic tumor; immunoprofile here (SMA, desmin, vimentin) points to smooth muscle differentiation, not pericytic

candidate_relations.label: Meningioma
candidate_relations.reason: Histology showed a malignant spindle cell neoplasm with smooth muscle markers, definitively excluding meningioma. Meningioma was only a pre-surgical clinical consideration.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Meningioma was the clinical pre-operative differential but histology confirmed a malignant spindle cell neoplasm inconsistent with meningioma

case_quality_flags: Intracranial/calvarial leiomyosarcoma is extremely rare; EBV-negative status noted, consistent with non-immunocompromised host smooth muscle tumor
Pre-operative clinical diagnosis of osteoblastic meningioma was overturned by histology
